name: terminal
title: The terminal
description: Gate B4 of an airport at the right, seen from above as a room in a game is: the truss and skylights of its ceiling, its glass wall onto the apron with a plane parked nose in, the split-flap board and the gate's sign hung in front of it, and on the carpet the gate desk and its queue, rows of seats with travellers, the coffee kiosk, a garden, the baggage carousel carrying the context window as suitcases, and a moving walkway; the jet bridge comes in through the west wall. Viktor, a Clawd, lives at the gate as the man in The Terminal did: crackers with ketchup and mustard, a can of Planters, his rug and his lamp, Krakozhia forever delayed. Outside, planes land and lift off on the runway at the horizon.
author: Solar Clawd
waits: Two lamps on the gate's sign hung over the desk, either side of its B4, and the board's CLAUDE row: the right lamp orange and the row BOARDING in orange while Claude asks, the lamp white and the row LANDED once it is done, both lamps orange with a wider, quicker glow and the row LAST CALL once a question has waited; Viktor gets up from his bench and faces the sign.
